name: National Bank of Umm Al Qaiwain
founded: 1982 (incorporated by Amiri Decree No. 1 of 5 Jan 1982; operations from 1 Aug 1982)
ownership_summary: Listed on ADX. The Government of Umm Al Qaiwain is the largest shareholder and promoter with 34.00% at 31 Dec 2025; other holders above 5%: Salem Abdullah Salem Al Hosani 13.29%, Abdul Wahed Al Rostamani Group LLC 10.11% and Abdulla Ahmed Abdulla Al Mousa 6.06%. Moody's (10 Jul 2026) still cites the 34% government stake.

shareholders.holder: Abdul Wahed Al Rostamani Group LLC

government_link: Yes: Government of Umm Al Qaiwain holds 34.00% (31 Dec 2025). The Chairman is the Crown Prince of Umm Al Qaiwain, and Al Mualla family members hold the chair and vice-chair seats (S3, S5). Balances with major shareholders included AED 6.55bn of deposits at 31 Dec 2025 (S3).
group_structure: Bank plus one subsidiary, Twin Towns Marketing Management (L.L.C.-SO), Dubai (S1, S3). It carried a small associate until 2025 (share of loss AED 257 thousand in 2025, nil in H1 2026). The Islamic window, open since 2005, stopped originating new business and is in run-off (S3 note 1; AGM 9 Mar 2026, S5).

subsidiaries.name: Twin Towns Marketing Management (L.L.C.-SO), Dubai
subsidiaries.activity: Marketing management (consolidated subsidiary; ownership % not checked)

footprint: UAE only: 9 branches, plus ATMs/CCDMs, mobile and online banking (30 Jun 2026, S1). Domestic market share about 0.4% of UAE banking assets (Moody's, Dec 2025, S9).
customer_segments: Wholesale/corporate (incl. government-related entities and large UAE groups), SME, and retail (salaried individuals, UAE nationals' loan schemes, cards). No affluent, priority or private banking tier found.
business_lines: Corporate and retail banking (51% of 2025 segment gross income) and treasury and investments (48%) (fact sheet, S8). Retail products: current, savings, Al Kanz, children's savings, call and fixed deposits; personal, auto and mortgage loans (incl. National Loans Scheme); credit and prepaid cards. Wholesale: transaction banking, trade finance, corporate finance, institutional banking, FX/treasury, syndication; Dubai RERA trustee bank for escrow accounts (Nov 2025). No investment, wealth or brokerage products for clients were found.

capabilities.wealth_summary: NBQ is a small (AED 24.1bn assets at 30 Jun 2026), corporate- and treasury-led bank in Umm Al Qaiwain with 9 branches and 439 staff. Retail banking is deposits, salary loans, mortgages and cards. The website shows no investment, wealth, priority or brokerage products. Its own large investment portfolio drives 'investment gains', but this is proprietary, not a client business. The Islamic window has stopped new business and is in run-off. Digital work in 2025-26 focused on a new retail mobile/internet banking platform, UAE Pass, Aani instant payments and Apple Wallet, with plans for core banking and treasury platform modernisation and Open Finance partnerships.

private_banking.detail: No private or priority banking proposition on the website or in the annual report.

asset_management.detail: No asset management business. Investment securities (AED 3.54bn at 30 Jun 2026) are the bank's own portfolio.

brokerage.detail: No brokerage subsidiary or client trading service found.

digital_investing.detail: Retail digital banking platform (mobile and internet) went live in 2025, but no investing features are described.

structured_products.detail: Treasury offers corporate FX forwards, split deals and money market instruments; no retail structured products found.

islamic_wealth.detail: The Islamic window (from 2005) stopped originating new business and is being run down; a Shari'ah executive member stays until the run-off is complete.

partners.what: Home financing for buyers of AYA Beachfront Residences, Umm Al Quwain
Joined the Aani instant payment platform

initiatives.what: New retail digital banking platform (mobile and internet) live; UAE Pass login; Aani; Apple Wallet extensions; cloud strategy prepared with a consultancy; loan origination modernisation due 2026; core banking and treasury platform modernisation planned; Open Finance programme
Accredited by Dubai RERA as trustee bank for real estate escrow accounts
AGM elected the 2026-2029 board and approved a 20% cash dividend (AED 400m); Islamic window confirmed closed and in run-off

opportunities: No client investment, wealth or brokerage offering at all (website menus and annual report, S3, S11), so any wealth proposition would be greenfield.
Deposit base grew 29% year on year to AED 17.1bn at 30 Jun 2026, and the bank says it will 'launch a slew of solutions' and pursue Open Finance partnerships in retail (S2, S3).
Core banking and treasury platform modernisation is planned, so the technology stack is being re-platformed (S3).
barriers: Very small retail franchise and no affluent segment; 439 staff and 9 branches (S3).
Strategy is corporate, treasury and digital-payments focused; no stated wealth ambition found (S2, S3).
Funding is concentrated, with large deposits from major shareholders (S3, S9).

discrepancies.detail: Integrated Report 2025 note 1 and the 9 Mar 2026 AGM say new Islamic business has stopped and the window is in run-off (S3, S5). The H1 2026 interim note 1 still says the Group 'carries out Islamic banking operations through Islamic banking window' (S1), and Moody's (Jul 2026) lists Islamic banking among services (S9). Islamic income rose to AED 32.7m in H1 2026 (S1).
discrepancies.resolution: Treated as run-off per the board decision and AGM; recorded islamic_wealth as 'No'. Rising Islamic income is unexplained.
